subject: Week of Nov 16: Rapid Pulse — Wins, Hotspots, and QBR action tracker
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: exec-staff@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Week of Nov 16: Rapid Pulse — Wins, Hotspots, and QBR action tracker

Team — quick pulse for the week. This is intentionally tight (wins / hotspots / asks) so we can keep the QBR prep focused. I attached the working action tracker (QBR_action_tracker_v3.xlsx) — I updated owners in the "Action" tab. Please review the asks and flag any timing constraints by EOD tomorrow.

Wins:
- Hosted API: reduced 99th-percentile latency on text-gen by ~12% after kernel tuning (metric: 99p TOKEN LAT). Marissa + infra team executed the rollout on 11/14.
- Dedicated: 2 new Dedicated contracts closed (one mid-market, one strategic) — adds ~$220k ARR. Sales noted predictable throughput requirement validated.

Hotspots / Risks:
- Acme integration: procurement pushed for an SLA exception (data residency + extended retention) — legal & security review in progress. See Acme item in tracker (row 8).
- Cache invalidation bug intermittently affecting reranking routes at high QPS — repro is flaky; working hypothesis: race in KV cache invalidation. Blocking for some customers; impact: increased token cost and tail latency.
- Offline evaluation gap: missing post-deploy evals for quantized variants (could introduce quality regressions).

Asks / Actions (owners noted):
- Marissa: provide short post-mortem for the cache invalidation (due: 11/18). Attach any reproducible logs to the tracker. (attachment: deployment-metrics.pdf)
- Vivek: approve SLA exception asks for Acme or route through Dedicated (decision needed by 11/19).
- Rishi: prioritize running the quantized A/B evals on the gated testset and report quality deltas (due: 11/20).
- Laura: confirm QBR time slot and approve customer slide deck outline.

Meeting tie-ins: I created a short QBR action tracker in Drive and added initial slide bullets — link below. I'll run a 30-min alignment on Thursday to review action statuses.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cQBR-pulse-2026
Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFRA-4321

Attachments: QBR_action_tracker_v3.xlsx

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Programs
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: exec-staff@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Week of Nov 16: Rapid Pulse — Wins, Hotspots, and QBR action tracker

Thanks Vanessa — quick clarifications and updates:

- Cache invalidation: opening note — root cause looks like concurrent write ordering from the global cache feeder during bursts. I attached a short metrics dump showing the correlation between feeder lag and error spikes (deployment-metrics.pdf).
- Acme: engineering notes that Acme is misconfiguring webhooks causing duplicate replay; procurement asked for a hard SLA window. I recommend we propose a scoped SLA that excludes customer-driven webhook retries until they confirm fix.

Action updates:
- I'll upload the initial repro and logs to INFRA-4321 by EOD.
- For the QBR, I suggest a single customer slide for Acme that calls out the remediation plan and proposed temporary SLA language. We should not promise permanent retention changes without security sign-off.

Attachment: deployment-metrics.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: exec-staff@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Week of Nov 16: Rapid Pulse — Wins, Hotspots, and QBR action tracker

Agree with Marissa's assessment. Two concrete asks from my side:

1) Acme SLA path: I prefer we avoid permanent SLA exceptions. Options: (a) route Acme to Dedicated for the initial contract and include a 90-day probation for extended retention, or (b) accept a scoped make-good (no retention change) plus a formal remediation plan with milestones. I need a one-paragraph recommendation to present to the exec sponsor by 11/19. Vanessa — can you draft the recommended approach?

2) Resource prioritization: the cache invalidation looks like a P1 for customers on reranking. Marissa — please estimate a 2-week mitigation plan (heads down) vs a band-aid fix we can ship in 3 days. If the mitigation needs cross-team heads, mark it in the tracker and I'll reallocate 0.5 FTE from platform reliability for two weeks.

Also: for the QBR, Laura — please confirm the 20-min customer deep-dive slot; I'd like to block 25 mins.

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 07:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Week of Nov 16: Rapid Pulse — Wins, Hotspots, and QBR action tracker

Thanks all — quick updates and owners assigned in the tracker: I updated the Acme row with the recommended approach (route to Dedicated + 90-day probation for extended retention) and added a one-paragraph summary for the exec sponsor. Vivek — please see the "Decision" tab; if you approve I will send the proposed language to Acme legal and loop security for sign-off (attachment: acme_sla_request.docx).

Marissa — thanks for the metrics; please mark the INFRA-4321 ticket with your mitigation estimate. I updated the tracker to request a 3-day band-aid target and a 2-week mitigation plan as options. If you confirm the 2-week effort, Vivek I will accept the 0.5 FTE reallocation you offered.

Rishi — added a dedicated run for the quantized A/B on the testset; please upload results to the tracker by 11/20.

Laura — can you confirm the QBR 25-min slot for the customer deep-dive? If confirmed, I'll finalize the slide and share with Sally (Acme) for alignment.

Next steps:
- I'll circulate an updated QBR slide deck draft on Wednesday (FYI: link in tracker).
- Thursday 11/19 at 10:00 PST — 30-min alignment to review outstanding actions. Calendar invite sent.

Attachments: acme_sla_request.docx, QBR_action_tracker_v3.xlsx
